title: The Spider-Man Bet

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: Okay — theaters just bet their whole year on one Spider-Man movie?

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Pretty much. Brand New Day opens July thirty-first, and it's tracking near a hundred-ninety million. Biggest opening of the year.

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: That sounds amazing though. Why's it a bet?

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Because AMC lost six hundred thirty-two million last year. And every extra hundred million at the box office only adds them eighteen.

viz.label: AMC NET LOSS — FY2025, SEC FILING

lines.speaker: jessica
lines.text: So they don't just want it big. They need it huge.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: And here's the catch: zero IMAX screens. Nolan's new movie locked every one of them for three weeks.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Four billion in debt, stock under two bucks. So this isn't a premiere. It's the whole bet.

caption: Theater chains lost hundreds of millions last year. Now the whole quarter rides on one July 31 opening. Here's the math behind the Spider-Man bet.
